query: For an AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy in its uniform, fine lamellar state, whose strength and plasticity remain below industrial application requirements, what single intervention could improve performance for fasteners exposed to extreme temperature fluctuations, long-term mechanical loading, room-temperature creep, and corrosive conditions? State the proposed intervention, mechanism, predicted outcome relative to the starting alloy, applicable operating and test boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with explicit falsification criteria.

generation.hypothesis: Adding a small amount of tungsten (~1–2 at.%) to the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy will form tungsten-enriched precipitates at the lamellar interfaces that improve resistance to cyclic thermal fluctuations, long-term mechanical loads, room-temperature creep, and corrosion.
generation.material_initial_state: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy in a uniform, fine lamellar state with performance below industrial standards.
generation.intervention: Minor compositional change by adding approximately 1–2 atomic percent tungsten to the alloy.
generation.conditions: The modified alloy is processed under the same conditions (casting and thermomechanical processing) to yield a fine lamellar structure and then exposed to service conditions including extreme temperature fluctuations, sustained mechanical loading, room-temperature creep testing, and corrosive environments.
generation.structural_mediator: The tungsten is expected to segregate to the lamellar interfaces, promoting the formation of fine, tungsten-rich precipitates or dispersion-hardened phases.
generation.mechanism: Wavelength-segregated tungsten-rich precipitates impede dislocation movement and grain boundary diffusion, thereby enhancing yield strength and creep resistance. Moreover, the formation of stable passive films associated with tungsten may improve corrosion resistance under aggressive environmental conditions.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the starting alloy, the tungsten-modified alloy should exhibit improved yield strength, reduced room-temperature creep rates, and enhanced corrosion resistance while maintaining acceptable ductility for fastener applications.
generation.baseline: Performance metrics (e.g., yield strength, creep rate, and corrosion rate) of the original AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy in its fine lamellar state.
generation.boundary: The improvements are expected to be valid under industrial fastener conditions with extreme thermal cycling, long-term mechanical loading, room-temperature creep, and corrosive exposures. If tungsten addition leads to excessive intermetallic formation or embrittlement outside these conditions, the benefit may be nullified.
generation.uncertainty: The optimal tungsten content and its distribution are uncertain, and there is potential for unintended effects such as reduced plasticity if tungsten segregation is not well-controlled.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples: one set of the baseline AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy and one set with an additional 1–2 at.% tungsten. Process both sets identically to produce a fine lamellar structure. Subject the samples to thermal cycling tests simulating extreme temperature fluctuations, extended tensile and creep tests at room temperature, and expose them to standardized corrosive environments (such as salt spray or NaCl immersion).
measurements: Yield strength and ductility (via tensile testing)
Corrosion rate (using electrochemical tests in corrosive media)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the tungsten-modified alloy does not demonstrate statistically significant improvements (e.g., >10% increase in yield strength, >20% reduction in creep rate, and measurable enhancement in corrosion resistance) over the baseline alloy, then the hypothesis is falsified.
